correctness.rationale: For a jump in cell phase v and offset u the exact error mark is w(v,u)=v−1_{u<v}. Its phase mean is u−1/2 and phase square mean u²−u+1/3; conditional Poisson variance decomposition and each U_i uniform yield λ/6+λ² Var(sum U_i)/n² for any coupling. For even n, (V,1−V) pairs force constant sum. Independent offsets assign each isolated jump an independently uniform mark; double-jump cell collision probability ≤λ²/(2n), and two-cell-block collision probability ≤λ²/n for paired design, yielding triangular compound-Poisson TV bounds. Shared U yields a conditionally uniform jump on [U−1,U], exactly resolution invariant. Direct independent rational uniform moments and 9 variance-order cases corroborate without proving the all-n theorem.

value.rationale: A natural numerical integration problem for a discontinuous random path: the dependence structure changes leading-order mean-square error even with unchanged uniform marginals, and an explicit attainable lower bound guides stratified sampling design. The distributional distinction prevents using variance alone as a full error description; this is a motivated exact coupling optimization rather than arbitrary finite slicing.
